caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for five model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four variants of SepLLM (n=64, n=64 with H, n=64 with H/T, and n=128). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with linear scaling and tick marks at 0.1 intervals. All lines begin near a loss value of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline within the first 20,000 iterations, after which the rate of decrease slows. The purple line for Vanilla ends at approximately 2.45 at 140,000 iterations. The blue line for StrmLLM (n=64) ends near 2.60. The orange line for SepLLM (n=64) ends near 2.51, the green line for SepLLM (n=64, H) ends near 2.52, the red line for SepLLM (n=64, H/T) ends near 2.49, and the dark blue line for SepLLM (n=128) ends near 2.55. All lines are solid with no markers, and each is distinguished by a unique color as indicated in the legend.
